outcome: Nothing found that settles or moves the problem since 26 January 2024: the only in-window items are a withdrawn integer-only claim (Kumar, arXiv:2411.03468, posted 5 Nov 2024, withdrawn by its author 18 Jun 2025), a forward-looking sentence in a 2025 journal paper (Moniri, published 31 Dec 2025), and a 2026 preprint on the negative base -3/2 (Lu and Zheng, arXiv:2603.16794, 17 Mar 2026); every source I read still treats the existence of a positive Z-number for 3/2 as open.
problem_asks: Statement as frozen: 'no real number x has the property that the fractional parts of x(3/2)^n are less than 1/2 for all positive integers n.' (1) Whether there exists a real x with {x(3/2)^n} < 1/2 for every positive integer n; the bullet asserts there is none (Mahler's conjecture). (2) The condition is a single universal quantifier over all positive integers n, so verifying finitely many n settles nothing, and a result for one residue class or one base-power subsequence is a restricted case. (3) Wording gap: the literal bullet ranges over all real x, including negative x and x = 0. x = 0 satisfies the condition trivially (its fractional parts are all 0 < 1/2), so the bullet as literally worded is false at x = 0. The literature (Mahler 1968, Strauch, Kumar) restricts to positive reals x > 0, called Z-numbers. I did not check whether any negative x has the property; no source I read addresses it. (4) Variant: Strauch and some others take n >= 0 instead of n >= 1; I did not treat this as changing the question.

events.what_happened: K. Mahler, 'An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2', J. Austral. Math. Soc. 8 (1968) 313-321. Poses the Z-number question (the problem was put to him by a Japanese colleague, per Mahler's own paper as quoted in a search snippet) and conjectures that no Z-numbers exist. Proves that the set of Z-numbers is at most countable, that there is at most one Z-number in each interval [n, n+1) for integer n >= 0 and it lies in its first half, and that there are at most about x^0.7 Z-numbers up to x. Also links existence in [n, n+1) to whether iterates of a Collatz-type map g avoid residue 3 mod 4 (secondary report). I read this only through secondary citations (Lagarias's survey page, CRC, Kumar's introduction, search snippets); the Cambridge PDF did not resolve.
events.delivers: Partial results only: countability of Z-numbers, at most one per unit interval [n, n+1) (in its first half), and an O(x^0.7) bound on how many Z-numbers lie below x. These bound how many Z-numbers there can be. None rules out a single Z-number and none produces one.
events.remains: Whether any positive real is a Z-number. That is the whole problem.
events.direction: The results are upper bounds on how many Z-numbers there can be, pointing toward the conjectured non-existence; the conjecture itself asserts non-existence.

events.what_happened: R. Tijdeman (spelled 'Tijdman' in the CRC and Lagarias references), 'Note on Mahler's 3/2-problem', Kongel. Norske Vidensk. Selsk. Skr. 16 (1972) 1-4. I did not read the note. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J., 2006) reports that a result of Tijdeman implies every number at least 3 lies in Dubickas's parity set Z (see the 2006 event), which is a different property from Mahler's condition.
events.delivers: Per Dubickas (2006, secondary): a result implying that every alpha >= 3 lies in the parity set Z. This does not reach alpha = 3/2, which is below 3. Whether the note says anything directly about 3/2 is not established.
events.remains: Everything for 3/2; Dubickas states Mahler's question for 3/2 remains open.
events.doubts: Unverified: the note was not read and its content is known only from a secondary report.
events.direction: Not stated for 3/2. The secondary report is about bases at least 3.

events.what_happened: L. Flatto, 'Z-numbers and beta-transformations', Symbolic Dynamics and its Applications, Contemp. Math. 135 (1992) 181-201. Listed in the CRC and Andrieu-Eliahou-Vivion references (the latter as 'Z_{p/q}-numbers (Flatto, 1992)'). I did not read it. A search snippet reports Flatto improved Mahler's counting bound to O(x^theta) with theta = log_2(3/2), about 0.59.
events.delivers: Per a secondary report only: an improved upper bound O(x^theta), theta = log_2(3/2), on the number of Z-numbers up to x. A counting bound, not existence.
events.remains: Existence or non-existence of a positive Z-number, i.e. the whole problem.
events.doubts: Unverified: not read; the exponent comes from a search snippet.
events.direction: Counting bound, pointing toward conjectured non-existence only indirectly.

events.what_happened: L. Flatto, J. C. Lagarias, A. D. Pollington, 'On the range of fractional parts {xi(p/q)^n}', Acta Arith. 70 (1995) 125-147 (DOI 10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147). Their Theorem 1.4, as quoted in Lu and Zheng (2026) and Kumar (2024), gives limsup minus liminf of {xi(p/q)^n} >= 1/p for every real xi > 0 and coprime integers p > q > 1. For 3/2 this is 1/3. Secondary sources state a bound on Omega(p/q) that does not agree with this (see doubts). The paper itself was not read: the IMPAN page gives only bibliographic data.
events.delivers: For the base 3/2: for every xi > 0, limsup minus liminf of {xi(3/2)^n} is at least 1/3, so no xi > 0 has its whole orbit inside an interval shorter than 1/3. The bound does not reach the window [0, 1/2) of the Z-number condition, which has length 1/2.
events.remains: Whether some xi > 0 has its whole orbit inside [0, 1/2), the Z-number question. The Wikipedia article's remark is that Mahler's conjecture would follow if Omega(3/2) exceeded 1/2; the 1/3 bound falls short of that threshold.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (refereeing inferred; not read)

checked_by.who: A. Dubickas (Vilnius) and Y. Bugeaud, per a search snippet on Lu-Zheng's introduction
checked_by.qualification: Specialists in fractional parts of powers
checked_by.what_they_did: Bugeaud and Dubickas gave a new, simpler proof and a generalisation to real algebraic numbers that are neither Pisot nor Salem (secondary report; not read)

events.doubts: Statement dispute, not an error found in the paper. Lu and Zheng (2026) and Kumar (2024) quote the 1/p form. The Wikipedia article (via a summarising fetch) states Omega(p/q) > 1/p. A search snippet quoting the Encyclopedia of Mathematics says Omega(p/q) > 1/q. For 3/2 that is 1/2, and the Wikipedia remark would then make the 1/q reading settle Mahler's conjecture for 3/2 in 1995. No 2024-2026 source says the problem was settled, so I weight the 1/p reading as correct. The EoM page returned HTTP 502 and I could not verify the 1/q wording.
events.direction: A lower bound on oscillation, consistent with the Z-number question's window being short; it does not exclude a Z-number.

events.what_happened: A. Dubickas, 'Even and odd integral parts of powers of a real number', Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006) 331-336 (DOI 10.1017/S0017089506003090). Defines a set Z inside (1, infinity): alpha is in Z if some nonzero real xi makes the integral parts [xi alpha^n] even for all n. States that Tijdeman's result implies every number at least 3 is in Z, and that Mahler's question whether 3/2 is in Z remains open. Shows the complement of Z in (1, infinity) is nonempty and gives explicit members of Z in (5/4, 3) and of the complement in (1, 2). I read the abstract and definition on the Cambridge page.
events.delivers: Not a result on Mahler's Z-numbers as such. It studies a parity set Z. For positive xi, {y} < 1/2 holds exactly when [2y] is even, so a positive Z-number xi for 3/2 gives 2xi with [2xi (3/2)^n] even; this equivalence is my inference, not stated in the source, and I did not check the sign-changing case. Establishes: complement of Z nonempty; explicit members in (5/4, 3) and in (1, 2). Nothing about 3/2.
events.remains: Membership of 3/2 in Z, which the author calls Mahler's open question.

checked_by.who: Glasgow Mathematical Journal (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (refereeing inferred; not read)

events.direction: Neutral on 3/2; it leaves Mahler's question open in its own words.

events.what_happened: S. Akiyama (with Frougny and Sakarovitch in the rational-base framework), a 2008 result, exact paper not identified: for coprime p > q > 1 with p > q^2, there is xi > 0 whose orbit {xi(p/q)^n} stays in a Cantor set for all n; the Hausdorff dimension is positive but tends to 0 as p grows with q fixed. Known only from a search snippet of a 2018 arXiv survey (arXiv:1806.03559). I did not read the primary.
events.delivers: An analogue for bases p/q with p > q^2. The base 3/2 does not satisfy p > q^2 (3 is not greater than 4), so this does not apply to Mahler's base and does not bear on the window [0, 1/2).
events.doubts: Unverified primary; the date and hypothesis come from a secondary snippet.
events.direction: Not about the problem's direction; a neighbouring class of bases.

events.what_happened: A. Dubickas, 'Powers of a rational number modulo 1 cannot lie in a small interval', Acta Arith. 137 (2009) 233-239 (DOI 10.4064/aa137-3-4). I read the bibliographic page only. Per Lu and Zheng (2026), quoting Dubickas's Theorems 1 and 2: for real xi != 0 and eta, and rational alpha = p/q with p > q >= 1 under a non-degeneracy condition, limsup minus liminf of {xi alpha^n + eta} is at least 1/p. Per a search snippet quoting Dubickas's introduction: the open question is whether the set of xi with orbit in an interval [s, s+1/p) is empty for each s; Bugeaud showed it is empty for almost all s in [0, 1-1/p]. Bugeaud's paper was not identified.
events.delivers: Generalises the 1/p oscillation bound to all real xi != 0 and eta and to rational bases p/q under a non-degeneracy condition. For 3/2 the gap is at least 1/3. The length-1/p window question for each starting point s is stated as open, with the almost-all-s partial result. The Z-number question has window length 1/2, so this window question is a different one.
events.remains: The length-1/p window question for every s, and the Z-number question for window [0, 1/2).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (refereeing inferred; not read)

events.doubts: The abstract was not read; the theorem statements are from Lu and Zheng's quotation and the Bugeaud claim from a search snippet. Bugeaud's a.e.-s result is not separately recorded because its paper and date were not found.
events.direction: Generalises a bound that is consistent with the Z-number question's window being too short to force a contradiction; does not decide the Z-number question.

events.what_happened: O. Strauch, 'Mahler's Conjecture on xi(3/2)^n mod 1', Uniform Distribution Theory 16(2) (2021, published 2 Feb 2022), pp. 49-70, DOI 10.2478/udt-2021-0007. Received 27 Feb 2019, accepted 29 Aug 2021, published 2 Feb 2022. Abstract read on the publisher mirror: if xi is a Z-number, then the sequence x_n = {xi(3/2)^n} has asymptotic distribution function c0 with c0(x) = 1 for x in (0, 1]. This is a conditional consequence of a hypothetical Z-number. A 2015 conference abstract by Strauch (PDF not readable; metadata Aug 2015) is reported by a search snippet to tie the conjecture to a functional equation for distribution functions; I did not read it. The date given is the earliest write-up date I can establish for the argument, which is the received date of the journal paper.
events.revisions: A 2015 conference abstract (not readable) predates the 2019 write-up; published in print 2 Feb 2022.
events.delivers: Conditional only: if a positive Z-number exists, its orbit's distribution function is c0 with c0 = 1 on (0, 1]. Establishes no existence or non-existence result.
events.remains: Whether a Z-number exists. The whole problem.

checked_by.who: Uniform Distribution Theory (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper on 29 Aug 2021 (publisher page); refereeing inferred; body not read

events.doubts: I read only the abstract, so I cannot say whether the body draws any further consequence that contradicts a Z-number's orbit.
events.direction: Necessary condition for a hypothetical Z-number; does not cut either way on existence.

events.what_happened: N. S. Kumar, 'Mahler's 3/2 problem in Z+', arXiv:2411.03468. Version 1 submitted 5 Nov 2024. Claims there are no Z-numbers among the positive integers. The ar5iv rendering (which I take to be v1, since v2 carries no text; not verified) gives the abstract, introduction, section headings and the closing step: sets X_n of positive integers with a permissible action are nested, their intersection is the residue class of 2^n mod 2^n, and 'Clearly, there is no positive integer which is divisible by every power of 2.' I did not check Lemma 4.7 or the rest of the argument. Version 2, submitted 18 Jun 2025, is a withdrawal notice with no text. The comment field says: 'The paper has an alternate proof method, but there are trivial ways to prove the same.'
events.revisions: v1 5 Nov 2024 (claim, 6 KB); v2 18 Jun 2025, withdrawn by author (1 KB, no text).
events.delivers: A restricted class: no Z-number among positive integers x, if the argument is correct. This does not touch non-integer positive reals, which make up almost all of the problem's domain. It does not touch x = 0 either.
events.remains: All positive reals x that are not integers, x = 0 and negative x (as the literal bullet covers), and the question for every positive real as the literature states it.
events.time_since_posted: 23 months from v1; withdrawn after 7 months
events.doubts: (1) Withdrawn by the author on 18 Jun 2025; no reason is given on the arXiv page. (2) The comment field itself says a different method exists and that 'trivial ways' prove the same. (3) I did not verify the nested-set argument, and the closing step as quoted is a short claim about residue classes. (4) I found no third-party reading or citation; the arXiv export page lists no citing papers, and I did not check external citation indexes.

withdrawn.what: Version 2 is a withdrawal: 'This paper has been withdrawn by Nikhil Kumar.' No reason is stated.

events.direction: Consistent with Mahler's conjecture (no Z-numbers), restricted to positive integers. If correct it is a restricted-class result, not a resolution of the bullet as stated.

events.what_happened: M. Moniri, 'Ramsey-Collatz Correlation and Some Extremal Combinatorics, along with Ramsey-Mahler Rare Concurrencies', Uniform Distribution Theory 20 (2025) 90-143, DOI 10.2478/udt-2025-0007. Submitted 7 Apr 2024, accepted 12 Nov 2024, published 31 Dec 2025. The abstract (read through a summarising fetch) studies a Ramsey-type labelling problem on ternary trees and reports a statistical correlation with Collatz stopping times. Its one Mahler sentence is forward-looking: 'Our next products additionally relate to Mahler's 3/2-problem and large stopping times showing a real number is not a Z-number.' No Mahler result is stated in the abstract. No arXiv preprint was found; the journal publication is the earliest public appearance I could locate.
events.delivers: Nothing is stated as established about Mahler's problem. The abstract announces future work toward 'large stopping times showing a real number is not a Z-number'.

checked_by.who: Uniform Distribution Theory (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted 12 Nov 2024 (publisher page). The Mahler sentence is not a claimed result, so acceptance does not speak to it.

events.doubts: The Mahler sentence is forward-looking and names no theorem. The full PDF was returned as binary by my tool, so I could not check whether the body contains a 'real number is not a Z-number' theorem. If it does, it is an event I have not captured and the record would need revision.
events.direction: Announced as future work toward showing that a real number is not a Z-number, i.e. toward non-existence; no direction is established.

events.what_happened: Q. Lu and W. Zheng, 'Fractional parts of powers of negative rationals', arXiv:2603.16794 (math.NT). For real xi != 0 and coprime p > q >= 1 (xi irrational or q > 1), the sequence xi(-p/q)^n mod 1 is not contained in any interval shorter than (1 + q/p - q^2/p^2)/p; for (p, q) = (3, 2) this is 11/27. The introduction (read through an HTML summary) quotes Flatto-Lagarias-Pollington Theorem 1.4 and Dubickas's theorems, and says of Mahler's question: 'One intriguing open question considered by Mahler [13] is the following: Does there exist a real number xi>0 such that {xi(3/2)^n}<1/2 for all n>=0?' and calls it open.
events.revisions: v1 17 Mar 2026; v2 24 Mar 2026; v3 17 Jun 2026; v4 4 Sep 2026 ('fixed typos').
events.delivers: An analogue, for the negative base -3/2 and sharper bounds for negative rational bases. It does not treat the positive base 3/2 of Mahler's question, so it bears on the problem only as an analogue.
events.remains: The whole positive-base question, which the introduction itself presents as open.
events.doubts: Not peer-reviewed as far as I can tell. Full text was returned as binary by my tool, so the body is known only from the HTML summary and abstract. Its object is a different question (negative base), so its strength is not a measure of the positive-base problem.
events.direction: Analogue for negative bases; no direction on the positive-base question.

disputes.summary: The Flatto-Lagarias-Pollington bound is quoted as limsup minus liminf >= 1/p (Lu and Zheng's Theorem 1.4 quote, Kumar's introduction, Dubickas via Lu and Zheng, and the Wikipedia summary) and as Omega(p/q) > 1/q (a search snippet of the Encyclopedia of Mathematics, page not readable). For 3/2 these give 1/3 and 1/2. Because the Wikipedia article says Mahler's conjecture would follow from Omega(3/2) > 1/2, the 1/q wording would settle the problem; no 2024-2026 source says it does, so I treat it as a misquotation, unverified.

Dubickas (2006) uses 'Z' for a different-looking set: alpha such that some nonzero xi makes [xi alpha^n] even for all n. For positive xi this corresponds to Mahler's condition up to doubling xi (my inference). The Glasgow abstract nonetheless treats 3/2's membership as the open Mahler question. Tijdeman's result, as Dubickas reports it, covers alpha >= 3 only.

The frozen bullet says 'no real number x'. Taken literally this includes x = 0, which satisfies the condition trivially, and negative x. The literature (Mahler 1968, Strauch, Kumar) restricts to positive reals. I did not check negative reals.

Mahler says the question came from 'a Japanese colleague'. One annotated 3x+1 bibliography attributes it to Saburo Uchiyama via a personal communication from S. Ando. No primary source confirms this; I did not read the bibliography entry directly.

summary: I ran 35 searches (listed verbatim below) and opened the primary or publisher pages for the main items. Mahler's problem is Mahler's 1968 conjecture that no positive real x has {x(3/2)^n} < 1/2 for all n. The Wikipedia article (last edited 10 March 2026) states it as an open problem, but I read it only through a summarising fetch, not verbatim. The sources I read all still treat existence as open: Strauch's 2022 paper (conditional result only), Lu and Zheng's 2026 introduction (calls Mahler's question open), and Andrieu, Eliahou and Vivion's 2025 paper, which treats the existence of Z-numbers as open and does not cite Kumar. In the window (after 26 January 2024) there are three items. (i) Kumar, arXiv:2411.03468, posted 5 Nov 2024, claims no Z-number among the positive integers; the author withdrew it on 18 June 2025 with no reason given. This is a restricted class, not a resolution of the bullet. (ii) Moniri, Uniform Distribution Theory 20 (2025), published 31 Dec 2025: a forward-looking sentence about 'showing a real number is not a Z-number', with no theorem named. I recorded it as an event with no claimed result, because it names this problem and I could not read the full PDF. (iii) Lu and Zheng, arXiv:2603.16794, 17 Mar 2026: a sharper bound for the negative base -3/2 (11/27 for (3,2)). This is an analogue, not the positive base. Older partial results are recorded as events. Mahler 1968 gives countability, at most one Z-number per [n, n+1), and an O(x^0.7) count. Flatto 1992 (secondary only) improves the count. Flatto-Lagarias-Pollington 1995 (Theorem 1.4 as quoted) gives an oscillation bound of 1/p, which is 1/3 for 3/2. Dubickas 2009 generalises that bound, and the length-1/p window question is open with a partial result for almost all starting points. Strauch's 2022 paper gives a conditional consequence. Close calls: (a) The Flatto-Lagarias-Pollington bound has conflicting statements. Most sources quote 1/p. A search snippet of the Encyclopedia of Mathematics says Omega(p/q) > 1/q, which would settle the problem for 3/2 via the Wikipedia remark. The EoM page returned HTTP 502, so I weight the 1/p reading as correct and flag the other. (b) Kumar's integer claim: recorded as an event because it is a claimed result, but its scope is a subset of the problem's domain, so I do not treat it as a resolution. (c) Moniri: recorded despite no stated result, because the sentence concerns this problem. (d) Dubickas's Z: the link to Mahler's condition is my inference. (e) The problem's literal wording includes x = 0, which trivially satisfies the condition, so the bullet as written is false at x = 0; the literature restricts to positive reals. AI: no source I opened credits any AI system with work on this problem, and the in-window authors name none in the parts I could read. The AI-specific searches found nothing on this problem. OpenAI's release of 722 manuscripts (6 Oct 2026; GitHub README read) has no Mahler 3/2 entry, and its only 'Mahler' family is 'Symmetric and general Mahler conjectures', which is a different problem I did not open. OpenAI's Astra announcement (1 Aug 2026, secondary coverage) lists ten advances, none on this problem. The Google DeepMind formal-conjectures code search was a login wall, so I could not check for a Lean entry.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a different reading is the Encyclopedia of Mathematics wording, Omega(p/q) > 1/q (via a search snippet). On that reading Omega(3/2) > 1/2, and by the Wikipedia remark Mahler's conjecture for 3/2 would follow from Flatto-Lagarias-Pollington 1995, so the problem would be settled in 1995 and every later source would be wrong to call it open. Against it: three sources quote the 1/p form, Lu and Zheng quote the theorem's inequality directly, and no source credits 1995 with a resolution. A second reading would count Kumar's integer result as a partial resolution of a problem about positive reals. That reading treats the positive integers as the problem, which they are not.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Flatto-Lagarias-Pollington 1995 paper: its Theorem 1.4 and the definition of Omega. The Acta Arithmetica page offers a free download. (2) The Encyclopedia of Mathematics Z-number page, when it is reachable. (3) Kumar's full v1 argument and any author statement on the withdrawal. (4) Moniri's full text, to check for any theorem about real numbers that are not Z-numbers. (5) Strauch's full body and any work citing Kumar. (6) Bugeaud's a.e.-s paper, which I did not identify. (7) A search of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures for a Mahler 3/2 entry, which needs a logged-in GitHub session.

events.credibility_reason: Withdrawn by the author on 18 Jun 2025 (arXiv v2); the integer case it claimed is in any case near-trivial per the author's own comment.

judgement.why: Only three events fall after 26 Jan 2024. Kumar's integer-only claim would be a case at most, but the author withdrew it, so it is knocked down. Moniri's abstract only announces future work, so it scores none. Lu-Zheng treats the negative base -3/2, which makes it a variant. The pre-snapshot events are counting bounds (Mahler, Flatto), the 1/3 oscillation bound (FLP 1995), a conditional consequence (Strauch), and results on other bases or parity sets (Tijdeman, Dubickas, Akiyama). None of them settles the question. The close call was FLP 1995 under the 1/q reading, which would make it a pre-snapshot resolution. The weight of quotations, plus every later source calling the problem open, supports 1/p, so I scored it as a bound. Dubickas 2009 extends the 1/p bound to other bases, and for 3/2 it gives the same 1/3, so I treated it as a variant and not a new bound. No AI was involved in any event.
judgement.doubts: The FLP 1995 1/p versus 1/q discrepancy is unresolved in the record. The literal statement is false at x = 0, while the literature restricts to x > 0; I judged against the positive-real reading. Moniri's full text was unread and might contain a result.
